## Completed example

**Question:** How can one university identify candidates at elevated risk of withdrawal early enough to offer support?
**Intended inference:** bounded prediction within that university, not universal causation.

| Criterion | Administrative prediction | Candidate interviews | Combined design |
|---|---|---|---|
| Supports | risk classification in the observed system | situated accounts of processes | bounded prediction plus explanation of selected cases |
| Cannot establish | causal mechanism or unrecorded experience | prevalence or predictive performance | causal effect without further design |
| Main risk | historical and coding bias | access and self-selection | integration, burden and scope |
| Cheap test | reproduce outcomes and inspect missingness | test recruitment and topic safety | test whether cases can be linked lawfully |
| Stop condition | outcome or timing cannot be reconstructed | recruitment route is unsafe or unavailable | no lawful, useful integration path |

**Provisional choice:** begin with an administrative feasibility audit. Proceed to the combined option only if lawful linkage, participant protection, recruitment and integration logic are confirmed.

## Scenario test

Option A is methodologically attractive but requires access that a collaborator has mentioned informally. Option B is narrower but feasible. Mark access for A as unverified—not available. Set a date and owner for written confirmation while testing B. Do not build the candidature plan around A until authority and practical access are evidenced.
